etymologies.etymologyHTML: Derived from GP, initialism of general-purpose. Noun from General Purpose Vehicle (military light utility truck).

definitions.definition: (military) Pertaining to utility or general purpose.
A small, blocky, military-style vehicle with four-wheel drive, suited to rough terrain.
A light utility truck from WWII used by the U.S. Army, and subsequently turned into the trademark Jeep when civilianized by originating manufacturer Willys-Overland.
(genericized trademark) A sport utility vehicle or similar four-wheel-drive vehicle.

quote.citation: 1997, John H. Esterline, Mae H. Esterline, Innocents Abroad: How We Won the Cold War, page 272:
quote.text: From there we jeeped over extraordinarily difficult roads to Marwari City, the site of Southern Philippine University, where I had been invited to address a convocation on the subject of "College Life in the United States."

etymologies.etymologyHTML: Disputed. Possibly from Eugene the Jeep, a character in Popeye cartoons.

definitions.definition: (corrosion) A device for detecting discontinuity in a protective coating, also called a "holiday detector"[2]
(Australia, regional) A covered shopping cart, also called a "shopping stroller".[3]

etymologies.etymologyHTML: An ironic pronunciation of AGP, the initialism of autogynephilia in Blanchard's transsexual typology.
